key_insight: Encoding conditions in the input state lets one shared IQP circuit represent conditional distributions beyond those achievable by diagonal conditioning with the same qubit count.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables classical training of conditional quantum generative models while sharing circuit parameters across conditions.
method: Encode each condition in the input state rather than in diagonal-layer parameters.
Apply a single shared IQP unitary across conditions.
Use efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude ratios to estimate conditional maximum mean discrepancy and gradients without bias.
evidence_signal: On the 16-qubit Curie–Weiss model, mean total variation distance was six times lower than diagonal conditioning at held-out temperatures; models up to 2048 qubits reproduced mean squared magnetization away from the crossover.
watch_item: Classical training requires efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation; large-scale moment agreement alone does not establish full-distribution accuracy or quantum advantage.
paper_title: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines
